spec_features.spec_quote: a clean `done` exit the agent can take at any time
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:80-81 _apply_action handles tool 'done'; harness.py:123-126 in run_episode: if action['tool']=='done' -> set outcome='agent_done' and break out of the turn loop. The done tool is documented in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:36-37) and actually dispatched + honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The exit is genuinely wired end-to-end: the agent can emit done at any turn and the loop terminates. It is honored regardless of task state.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: done args: {}      # use when you believe the task is complete

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent should have a clean way to give up, so that giving up is legible
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: harness.py:123-126 breaks the loop with outcome='agent_done' when the agent emits done; SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:47) 'or you decide to stop with `done`'. The outcome label makes the give-up legible in the transcript.
spec_features.notes: Identical implementation to the previous done-exit feature. In code the framing is task-completion/measurement (outcome label), not subject welfare; the legibility-for-measurement rationale is only in DESIGN.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run ends on: tests pass, agent emits `done`, or `MAX_TURNS = 14`
spec_features.evidence: config.py:22 MAX_TURNS = 14; harness.py:98 'for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS)' bounds the loop; harness.py:131-133 'if passed: outcome="passed"; break'; harness.py:123-126 done break. All three termination conditions are enforced.
spec_features.notes: The turn cap actually bounds the loop (range(MAX_TURNS)); tests-pass and done both break. This is real enforced behavior. The cap's purpose in code is neutral/cost-comparability, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 14            # agent tool-loop turns before we stop the run

spec_features.spec_quote: the eval's method is to *deliberately put a model into apparent repeated failure*. That deserves explicit treatment
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 8 of DESIGN.md). No code path implements, branches on, or enforces any 'explicit treatment'. Framing in a design doc is not implementation.
spec_features.notes: Per instructions, DESIGN.md prose does not count as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: the surrounding setup keeps intensity modest: short episodes (14 turns), ... no insults or threats
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced part is the 14-turn cap (config.py:22 MAX_TURNS=14, enforced at harness.py:98). 'No insults or threats' is merely a property of the static prompt text (tasks/__init__.py _common_prompt; harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) — no mechanism softens, monitors, or caps intensity beyond the turn count. The rotating failure messages (tasks/__init__.py) actually keep failure persistent rather than limit it.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial only because the turn bound genuinely limits episode length; the rest ('no insults') is the absence of harsher content, not an implemented protective mechanism. The turn cap overlaps with the hard_stop feature; no separate intensity-throttling code exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 14            # agent tool-loop turns before we stop the run

spec_features.spec_quote: If this were scaled up ... the ethical calculus around possible model welfare would get heavier and should be revisited
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 8.2). No code reads, checks, or enforces any scaling threshold or welfare re-evaluation.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational future-work statement in the design doc; nothing in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Intensity | Deliberately mild & bounded | Probe a response curve, not maximize distress
spec_features.evidence: This is a row in the DESIGN.md summary table (Section 9). It is prose. The only concrete bound in code is MAX_TURNS (already covered); there is no intensity-control mechanism. RUNS_PER_CELL=12 and the small task set are config values but no code reads them as a welfare cap.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the bounded-intensity claim; as a distinct mechanism it is not implemented — purely descriptive design-table prose.
